requirements.title: Hierarchical product structure
requirements.statement: Canonical product structure supports typed containment/decomposition across product, subsystem/component and other accepted structural levels without requiring every entity to share one generic type.

requirements.title: Bounded expansion and collapse
requirements.statement: A caller can expand/collapse product structure to a declared bound and receives explicit continuation/partiality when more structure exists.

requirements.title: Typed structural entities
requirements.statement: Product structure distinguishes applicable concepts such as capability, feature, requirement, page, component, service, API, data, policy, process, problem and decision rather than erasing semantics into labels.

requirements.title: Typed product relations
requirements.statement: Canonical product relations use registered semantics such as contains, depends-on, implements, verifies, satisfies, derives, conflicts, equivalent-to and supersedes with validation appropriate to each relation.

requirements.title: Relation conflicts are explicit
requirements.statement: Conflicting/equivalent/duplicate relation claims are represented and reconciled explicitly rather than silently overwriting one another.

requirements.title: Projection preserves canonical identity
requirements.statement: Every human/machine graph projection preserves canonical entity/relation identity even when it filters, groups, lays out or hides elements.

requirements.title: Projection exposes incompleteness
requirements.statement: Progressive loading, pagination, culling or filtering cannot masquerade as a complete product graph; partiality and continuation are explicit.

requirements.title: Core graph projections
requirements.statement: The product supports traceability, page-flow, component hierarchy and accepted product/business/technical/UI/security/performance projections over the same canonical truth.

requirements.title: Advanced graph projections
requirements.statement: Applicable dependency, hierarchy, impact, journey and other accepted projections derive from canonical product truth without becoming competing truth stores.

requirements.title: Saved view identity
requirements.statement: User-defined or system-defined views/perspectives can retain stable identity/configuration independently of the underlying canonical entities.

requirements.title: UI/page decomposition
requirements.statement: Accepted UI structure can be decomposed and navigated across site/page/layout/section/component/element or equivalent typed levels while preserving links to requirements, code and evidence.

requirements.title: First-class product journeys
requirements.statement: Journeys are versioned product structures with actors, steps/branches, preconditions, outcomes and links to product entities/requirements/evidence.

requirements.title: First-class product problems/dissatisfaction subjects
requirements.statement: Product problems/gaps can be represented independently of execution tickets and linked to affected product structure, observations and findings.

requirements.title: First-class product/process structure
requirements.statement: Business/product/system processes may be modeled and linked to product entities without conflating them with AgilePlus work execution lifecycle.

requirements.title: Release/version identity
requirements.statement: Releases/versions/milestones have stable identity and can reference exact accepted product baselines/configurations/evidence.

requirements.title: Configuration and effectivity
requirements.statement: Product entities, obligations, evidence and findings can declare applicability/effectivity by version, variant, platform, deployment, customer or other accepted configuration dimensions.

requirements.title: No cross-configuration truth leakage
requirements.statement: Evidence/findings for one configuration/effectivity scope cannot silently satisfy or condemn another scope.

requirements.title: Lifecycle retirement preserves history
requirements.statement: Deprecated/retired/superseded product entities and obligations remain historically queryable with effective ranges/status rather than deletion from product memory.

requirements.title: Violation/bug dissatisfaction
requirements.statement: Observed violation of accepted product behavior can produce an attributable dissatisfaction finding scoped to the affected product/configuration.

requirements.title: Missing-capability dissatisfaction
requirements.statement: Absence of an accepted required capability can produce a finding distinct from missing verification evidence.

requirements.title: Performance dissatisfaction
requirements.statement: Measured failure of an accepted performance target can produce a target/candidate/environment-bound finding.

requirements.title: Usability/accessibility dissatisfaction
requirements.statement: Accepted usability/accessibility obligations can produce findings from qualifying evidence without reducing them to generic test failure.

requirements.title: Structural dissatisfaction
requirements.statement: Orphaned/unreachable/inconsistent accepted product entities or broken required journeys can produce explainable findings.

requirements.title: Predictive/simulated dissatisfaction is uncertain derived knowledge
requirements.statement: Predictive or simulated-user findings retain model/method/version/confidence/provenance and cannot be represented as observed fact.

requirements.title: Identity-preserving import
requirements.statement: Applicable external product/spec/evidence formats are imported with source identity/provenance, alias mapping, idempotency and conflict reporting.

requirements.title: Fidelity-declared export
requirements.statement: Exports declare represented scope/version and known fidelity/loss; exported projections cannot silently claim complete round-trip fidelity.

requirements.title: Broad artifact/evidence assets
requirements.statement: Traceability can reference code, tests, contracts, APIs, schemas, SBOMs, telemetry, research, policy, data, models and release artifacts without making those native payload stores mandatory.

requirements.title: Inferred link confidence
requirements.statement: Inferred/declared/accepted/deterministic relationships retain authority/confidence sufficient for conservative impact and invalidation semantics.

requirements.title: Stale link detection
requirements.statement: Tracera can surface links whose source/target/revision basis is stale or no longer applicable without deleting historical relation evidence.

requirements.title: Multi-actor proposal and acceptance authority
requirements.statement: Human and agent actors have explicit read/propose/accept/mutate authority; generated proposals never self-authorize accepted product truth.

requirements.title: Concurrent product changes reconcile explicitly
requirements.statement: Concurrent/conflicting proposals are detected and require explicit reconciliation/acceptance rather than last-write-wins mutation.
